items.markdown:
Retatrutide works as a **triple-receptor agonist** , meaning it mimics and activates three distinct metabolic hormones in the body: **GLP-1**, **GIP** , and **glucagon**.[[1]](https://medical.lilly.com/us/products/answers/what-is-the-mechanism-of-action-of-retatrutide-301926)[[2]](https://www.incarenow.com/how-does-retatrutide-actually-work-inside-the-body/)[[3]](https://www.weightwatchers.com/us/blog/what-is-retatrutide)

Unlike older single-agonist drugs (like [Ozempic](https://www.uchealth.org/today/retatrutide-for-weight-loss/) / Wegovy) that only target GLP-1 or dual-agonist drugs (like Zepbound / Mounjaro) that target GLP-1 and GIP, retatrutide's triple-action approach combines appetite suppression, blood sugar regulation, and increased energy expenditure.[[1]](https://www.uchealth.org/today/retatrutide-for-weight-loss/)[[2]](https://www.incarenow.com/how-does-retatrutide-actually-work-inside-the-body/)



---

### How the Three Receptors Work

- **GLP-1 (Glucagon-Like Peptide-1) Receptor:** 
	- Slows down digestion and gastric emptying.
	- Promotes a feeling of fullness and significantly reduces appetite and food cravings.
	- Stimulates insulin secretion from the pancreas to lower blood sugar levels.[[1]](https://synapse.patsnap.com/article/what-is-the-mechanism-of-action-of-retatrutide)[[2]](https://www.weightwatchers.com/us/blog/what-is-retatrutide)[[3]](https://onlinedoctor.superdrug.com/retatrutide.html)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v4yYFJCchT8&t=93)
- **GIP (Glucose-Dependent Insulinotropic Polypeptide) Receptor:** 
	- Enhances insulin release and improves glucose homeostasis.
	- Works alongside GLP-1 to further curb food intake and optimize metabolic regulation.
	- Retatrutide is especially potent at activating the GIP receptor (roughly 8.9 times more potent than natural GIP).[[1]](https://onlinedoctor.superdrug.com/retatrutide.html)[[2]](https://medical.lilly.com/us/products/answers/what-is-the-mechanism-of-action-of-retatrutide-301926)[[3]](https://www.weightwatchers.com/us/blog/what-is-retatrutide)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v4yYFJCchT8&t=93)[[5]](https://www.incarenow.com/how-does-retatrutide-actually-work-inside-the-body/)
- **Glucagon (GCG) Receptor:** 
	- Stimulates the breakdown of stored fat (lipolysis and fatty acid oxidation).
	- Increases energy expenditure (calorie burning) rather than just lowering calorie intake.
	- Helps break down fat deposits in the liver and supports metabolic health.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=04dt_3ksaLk&t=228)[[2]](https://onlinedoctor.superdrug.com/retatrutide.html)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/f1vQVytu8Ho)[[4]](https://www.incarenow.com/how-does-retatrutide-actually-work-inside-the-body/)[[5]](https://www.weightwatchers.com/us/blog/what-is-retatrutide)[[6]](https://www.theindependentpharmacy.co.uk/weight-loss/guides/what-is-retatrutide)



---

### Current Status

- **Investigational Drug:** Retatrutide is developed by [Eli Lilly](https://medical.lilly.com/us/products/answers/what-is-the-mechanism-of-action-of-retatrutide-301926) and is currently undergoing late-stage clinical trials (Phase 3).
- **Not FDA-Approved:** As of 2026, it is **not yet approved** by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for routine prescription use.[[1]](https://www.weightwatchers.com/us/blog/what-is-retatrutide)[[2]](https://medical.lilly.com/us/products/answers/what-is-the-mechanism-of-action-of-retatrutide-301926)[[3]](https://onlinedoctor.superdrug.com/retatrutide.html)[[4]](https://www.incarenow.com/how-does-retatrutide-actually-work-inside-the-body/)
